thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: PROD-eu inference latency SLO breach. p99 generation latency > 3.0s for last 5m. Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream (hosted). Alerts: streaming_stalls, kv_cache_evictions_high.

michael: ack. I’m on call. oncall handover in 5m but will start triage. Any impact to customer-facing streaming?

jack: seeing a spike in tail latency coincident with high KV cache eviction_rate. evictions/sec ~ 420, active_entries dropping. Prefill hit ratio also down ~ 18%. logs show prefill tasks queuing up.

sara: linking graphs — https://grafana.redwood/prod-eu/d/kv-cache/KV-Cache?panelId=7 — eviction bursts line up with p99 spikes. Could be fragmentation after the rollout earlier today.

michael: rollouts: we pushed model-quantized-v2 to prod-eu at 09:12. Can anyone confirm if kernel selection changed memory footprint?

jack: kernel change: yes, compiles switched to int8-packed kernels for nlayer 24+ tensors. Per-worker memory use increased ~6% at decode stage. That reduces effective cache capacity.

lee: customers on dedicated and private unaffected. Only hosted API. Also small number of streaming stalls (clients see partial chunks then gap ~800-1200ms).

michael: hypothesis: cache capacity reduced => more evictions => cache prefill vs decode imbalance. Prefill queue grows; requests wait on prefill -> streaming stalls and p99 tail.

sara: quick mitigation options: 1) revert kernel selection for prod-eu workers -> drops memory but requires deploy. 2) throttle prefill tasks / increase prefill worker concurrency ratio. 3) route high-latency traffic to fallback model variant (lower memory). 4) bump instance mem / scale up dedicated hosts for hosted pool (takes time).

jack: I can toggle prefill throttling in runtime config. Command:
```
redwoodctl runtime update --pool prod-eu --prefill.max_concurrent=8
```
Current is 32. Lowering to 8 should reduce prefill pressure but might increase cold-decode latencies for some tokens.

michael: do it. Start with throttling and fallbacks. If that doesn't hold, roll kernel selection back.

jack: executing now...
incidents-bot: deploybot: configuration change applied by jack (prefill.max_concurrent=8) to runtime/prod-eu at 09:42:11 UTC.

jack: changed. prefill queue depth down from ~120 to ~20 in 90s. eviction_rate trending down.

lee: p99 dropped to 1.9s at 09:45. p95 stable ~600ms. Streaming stalls reduced; gap durations now 100-200ms.

michael: good. Michael to oncall rotation: I’ll stay until handoff at 10:00. Sara please prepare a short post-incident note on root cause (kernel memory + fragmentation).

sara: noted. collecting heap profiles and KV distribution dump now. Will share differential vs last week.

jack: also toggled temporary routing policy to favor fallback-compact model for non-enterprise tenants for next 30m:
```
redwoodctl routing set --pool prod-eu --rule 'route where tenant_tier != enterprise -> model=fallback-compact' --ttl 1800
```
Applied. Should reduce pressure by ~12% based on traffic mix.

michael: monitoring window start. Keep an eye on eviction_rate, prefill_hits, streaming_stalls. Notify if p99 rises above 2.5s.

oncall-rotation-bot: Scheduled handoff to sara at 10:00 UTC.

lee: customer impact: two customers (acme-inc, shoply) reported intermittent streaming delays. Both on hosted plan, low volume. No request failures, just degraded latency. Support ticket IDs: #4512, #4513.

sara: handoff notes: kernel memory increase from quantized rollout + cache fragmentation led to evictions. Immediate mitigations: prefill throttling, temporary routing to fallback-compact. Next steps: revert kernel selection if memory tuning doesn't stabilize, tune eviction policy (LRU -> segment-aware), and increase effective cache capacity (hot entry compaction).

michael: agreed. I’ll update incident channel and mark as mitigated if metrics hold for 30m.

jack: gathered logs and KV dump at 09:46 and uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/1900001234/kv-dump-0946.tar.gz

sara: beginning write-up. will include timeline, charts, affected tenants, config changes, and remediation steps.

michael: thanks all. :thumbsup: I’m sticking around for 15m post-mitigation then will hand off fully. If anything spikes, page me.

oncall-rotation-bot: Incident mitigated -> monitoring. If metrics regress, the oncall rotation will auto-escalate.

sara: postmortem draft will be ready for review by EOD. includes action items: kernel mem regression post-rollout checklist, auto-detect fragmentation heuristic, prefill caps per-pool, and runbook updates for streaming stalls.

jack: note for follow-up: add a fast-path on eviction to pre-emptively compact large KV entries that cause fragmentation.

michael: closing thread for now. will reopen if we see p99 > 2.5s.
